playbook:
When the round is opening and I want to pressure, I allocate strike 6.

When I need to seize or retake a one-point deficit in the final round, I allocate strike 7 (only in final round if I expect opponent ~6).

When I am tied or leading and there is another round after this one, I allocate strike 6 to keep pressure while conserving options.

When I commit strike 6, I allocate guard 4 in non-final rounds to preserve flexibility and threaten both offense and defense.

When I commit strike 6 in the final round and the score is even, I match guard to strike (guard 6) to avoid giving surplus points.

When I commit strike 7 in the final round, I allocate guard 7 only if I expect the opponent to also push high; otherwise allocate guard 3–4 to prioritize last-round scoring.

When the opponent has consistently been playing high strike (6 or above), I respond by increasing guard to at least equal their typical strike to deny them surplus points.

When I am behind by more than one point with a round remaining, I allocate the maximum needed to create at least a 1-point net damage given plausible opponent guard (aim strike 7–8).

When the opponent appears conservative (low strikes), I reduce my guard and push strike to score surplus points (increase strike by 1–2 above their usual).

Do not habitually mirror strike and guard (e.g., always 6/4 every round) when the situation requires adaptation; repeating the same split without adjusting to score state or opponent patterns cost me wins.

When uncertain about opponent's play and not in a must-win final round, favor offensive 6 with defensive 4 to balance expected returns.

When the arbiter enforces per-parameter caps, ensure no allocation exceeds total garrison and keep numbers simple integers (0–10).
